correctness.rationale: The bilinear common-edge objective matches the invariant. Extreme-point linear programming reduces both vertex-law supports to at most three; the affine-face quadratic argument proves an optimum must occur among zero-dimensional or negative-definite stationary candidates. Exact Q(sqrt(2)) elimination over all 920 symmetry-reduced support pairs gives 126 candidates and maximum (26-7sqrt(2))/32, with a fully checked explicit attaining 2+3-support witness. For separate mean-zero balance, exact enumeration gives 12 extreme distributions and 144 checked pairs, maximum 1/2. These critical code operations were inspected and the included standalone verifier was executed successfully.

value.rationale: Rainbow pushability is newly motivated by colorful geometric transversal theorems, and the initiating work invites exact values on further centered polytopes. The octagon is the next canonical centrally symmetric polygon after the square and hexagon. Its exact irrational optimum sits strictly above the intuitive 1/2 threshold, while the individually balanced optimum equals 1/2. This resolves a natural invariant and identifies a substantive difference between collective and individual balance, with explicit optimizers and a reproducible exhaustive certificate. It is not just an isolated numeric approximation.
